The form reloads to version 2 with '[restricted:2:1]'. Save 2 (If-Match 2) gives 200, stores [S, Q], and the form is at version 3: F-DG6-580 is fixed. B (EN and AR): 409. The form reloads to version 4 and shows 'This rule changed after you opened it. The form now shows the current version: re-apply your change, then save the draft again.' / 'تغيّرت هذه القاعدة بعد أن فتحتها …'. S is kept. C (EN and AR): the dry run passes, then submit, the TO's review and publish. v1 is at row version 4 and shows S as '[restricted:4:2]' with the lock label. Draft v2, after removing S and three saves, is [P, H] at row version 4 and shows H as '[restricted:4:2]', the identical text. Pasting v1's token gives 200, and v2 is stored as [P, H, H]. The screen shows two lock labels ('[restricted:5:2]', '[restricted:5:3]') before and after a reload, and S is not restored: F-DG6-640 (Medium). Run 4 is the result.

checks_run.actual: Accepted, unchanged since round 9 (the BE-Z14 diff touches none of them): D-194 to D-196 (plan and scope), D-199 (2) (the load dataset, disclosed), D-202, and D-203 (batch 8, concurrency 4, configurable). D-204: a late event is evaluated against the rule version in force and enabled at its occurrence. That keeps automation explainable and matches REQ-S12-019 and REQ-S20-013. D-205: a rule disabled now stops its pending events. The residual commit-order race in ADR-0043 can only run an action a person already enabled, never an approval or a gate, so it is acceptable as documented. D-231/D-232: the digest read (getMyNotificationDigest) now applies the same redaction as the inbox, and the guard fails on a new unredacted serializer. Accepted. The editor reload is accepted. The version binding is accepted for a single draft row, but challenged: the token carries only a row-version number. Row versions are small per-row counters, so a published version (row version 4 after create, submit, review and publish) and its draft after three saves issue identical token text for different records. A token copied from the published version (or from another rule) silently resolves to the draft's own hidden literal: F-DG6-640 (Medium). D-229 (connector configuration names stay cannot-name): accepted. credential_refs and field_mappings are written and read only by IT's manifest or by connector administrators, and the a17 and connectors suites show credentials are references only. D-228 (4) (cross-organization ids out of scope): accepted. A12 isolation passes in EN and AR, and each reach helper checks the reader's organizations first. No engineering agent and no assistant path grants a business, Finance or IT approval, and product G6 is not linked to DG7.

summary: FAIL. F-DG6-580 is CLOSED_VERIFIED. Its round-9 API and real-UI reproductions now give 422 restricted_token_stale (API) or a correct form reload (UI) in EN and AR, with S kept. A 409 shows the bilingual re-apply alert. Two revert mutants are caught by the candidate's own tests. New F-DG6-640 (Medium, REQ-S10-002): the D-231 token carries only a row-version number, which is not unique across version rows. A token copied from the published version 1 page into draft 2 at the same row version (4) resolves to the draft's own hidden literal H instead of S. The result is stored [P, H, H] with two lock labels on screen (real UI, real publish flow, EN and AR). Rule-to-rule pastes behave the same way. Everything else I ran passes: 97 register integration files (1226 tests), domain e2e (176 + 88, with 18 disclosed axe skips), web unit (137) and the serializer guard, the validators and the build. Each disclosed failure is explained: the probe's by-design soft assertions, an OOM-killed vitest fork, ENOSPC and probe-setup failures in early probe runs.
